It considers changes such as probing, endgame defection, and adapting to opponent types to improve cumulative score.

--- PART 2/6 ---
ORIGIN: NONE

STRATEGY: The parent is a mostly-cooperative strategy with a 5% exploit and no endgame defection; the trace simulates its last two rounds against 12 population slots; it compares defecting vs cooperating at round 99 (then defecting at 100) and considers probing at round 98.

--- PART 3/6 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Given the population, many are forgiving (slot2,5,6,9, parent)." and "The parent does something like that." and "Parent slot3 weaknesses:"
STRATEGY: The parent (slot3) cooperates first 5, defects if opponent defected >=7 in last 10, cooperates if <=2, otherwise uses TFT logic with occasional forgiveness/exploitation. The trace simulates the parent and other slots (slot0–slot11) against a probe-and-exploit endgame, computing payoffs for defecting vs cooperating at rounds 98–100. It proposes revising toward a probe-at-round-11 strategy that exploits forgiving opponents and falls back to TFT against retaliators.
